verdict: Strong, well-sourced structure with honest framing of the leaderboard claims, but it is far too dense for the ear: break up the number-stacked sentences, add pauses throughout, and stop the first story repeating the hook before we record.

worst_three.problem: The view and the whole bottom line run well over 200 words with no breath, so the listener loses the thread exactly where the episode lands its argument.
worst_three.fix: Insert [Pause] after 'every maker sets its own exam.', after 'not a verdict.', after 'where does your data live?', after 'this region is writing that chapter itself.', and between each of the three bottom-line points; apply the same rule across the script so no stretch exceeds 60 words.

worst_three.problem: The listener hears the 0.5% statistic from the hook a second time and feels the episode is going in circles before it has started.
worst_three.fix: Replace with: 'The Fanar 2.0 paper from QCRI, Qatar's computing research institute, is the source for that half-percent figure. And it is the root of everything else in this story.' Then move straight to Preslav Nakov's quote.

worst_three.problem: Sentences packed with dates and three model sizes, like this one and the Jais 2 and Jais 3 lines, blur into noise on a phone speaker.
worst_three.fix: Split each one, for example: 'Falcon-H1 Arabic followed in January 2026. It comes in three sizes, the largest at 34 billion parameters.' Likewise: 'Jais 2 arrived in December 2025. The largest version has 70 billion parameters.' Keep the full figures on the on-screen text only.
